Hi Olivia, Priyom —

Below is a short, copy-paste friendly summary you can use in your questionnaire. Where possible I've noted the configurable options and expected timelines.

Default retention (hosted API) — high level
- Raw requests / prompt text: retained by default for 45 days. This includes complete prompt payloads submitted to the API unless the customer opts into a shorter retention via an account setting or a dedicated/private deployment.
- Model-generated final outputs (responses): retained by default for 90 days for debugging, quality monitoring, and evals. Customers can request a shorter window; Dedicated/Private deployments can set different defaults per contract.
- Streaming fragments (intermediate tokens): not persisted by default. Streaming buffers are transient at the runtime layer and are discarded once a session is closed or the response is finalized. If a customer explicitly enables session capture/recording, fragments are then treated as part of the request/response artifact and inherit the request retention window.
- Embeddings & derived artifacts: treated as persisted artifacts and follow the same retention as stored outputs unless explicitly configured otherwise.
- Runtime KV caches: considered ephemeral optimization layers. By default KV cache contents are not stored in long-term logs; they are kept in-memory or short-lived storage for up to 7 days for warm-start purposes, but they are not part of the standard persisted audit trail unless the customer enables export.

Erasure / proof-of-deletion (what we provide)
- Erasure path: customer submits a deletion request via the Console or Support. We perform a two-phase removal: (1) mark records as deleted (tombstone) and schedule background purge jobs, (2) run physical deletion and update downstream storage indexes.
- Evidence provided: a generated erasure report that contains deletion request ID, ISO timestamps for request/starting/completion, counts of matched records removed (where applicable), and an audit trace ID you can reference for our internal logs.
- Timeline: typical SLA to produce deletion evidence is 3–5 business days after request acceptance for hosted customers. For large exports or accounts with long persistence windows, full physical purge can take longer (we'll provide an expected completion ETA in the erasure report).
- Scope: erasure covers persisted request bodies, stored outputs, and attachments that are part of the persisted artifact store. Runtime-only artifacts (transient streaming buffers, non-exported KV caches) are not part of persisted stores and therefore do not require a deletion job unless session capture was enabled.

Notes and exceptions
- EU residency: for customers with EU-only residency enabled, both retention and erasure are executed within the EU region and we include region-scoped audit evidence.
- Dedicated/Private: customers on Dedicated or Private plans can negotiate alternate retention windows and faster erasure SLAs in their contract; the mechanics are the same but the schedule/automation can differ.

Links: I've put a short runbook and our data map on Drive here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-redwood-data-map

Happy to tighten any phrasing for procurement language.

— Kimberly
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference

2) If KV caches are not part of the persisted audit trail by default, is there any scenario where they would be captured (e.g., platform debugging, support investigations)? If so, how is that documented and controlled?

Also, what's the expected acknowledgement we get when the purge is scheduled vs when it's fully complete? Procurement typically needs both dates.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Matthews <olivia@clearview.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-15T13:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify default retention for procurement review

Hi Olivia — quick clarifications to Kimberly's note:

- Attachments: yes — files uploaded as part of a request are stored in our object store and inherit the output retention window (90 days by default). They are included in erasure runs and will be listed in the erasure report by filename and byte counts when available.
- KV caches & debugging captures: KV caches used by the runtime are ephemeral by design and not included in persisted audit logs. The only times we capture runtime state outside the normal persisted artifacts are: (a) when a customer explicitly opts-in to session capture/recording, or (b) when we perform a signed troubleshooting snapshot with customer authorization (we log this and produce an opt-in record). Any such captures are tracked and can be audited; we only take them with explicit consent or as allowed by your contract.
- Acknowledgements / schedule: when you submit an erasure request we return a deletion request ID and an initial scheduled start timestamp (within 24 hours). The erasure report we send upon completion contains the completion timestamp and the counts. If you need both dates in a specific format for procurement, we can include UTC ISO timestamps in the final report.

I'll attach our internal erasure-runbook summary for reference (redacted for procurement).

— Karthik
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
